docRequirement: memory.md:99 binds the CLAUDE.md/memory `@path/to/import` scanner to Markdown awareness: "Import parsing skips Markdown code spans and fenced code blocks. To mention a path in your CLAUDE.md without importing it, wrap it in backticks: writing `` `@README` `` keeps the text literal, while `@README` outside backticks imports the file." The same section (memory.md:101) says imports are recognised "anywhere in your CLAUDE.md", and its own illustration is a fenced ```text block whose body lines are imports — i.e. a fenced `@path` line must be left as literal text.
current: No markdown-document state exists anywhere in the memory-import path. `parseMemoryImportPath` (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:49-64) is a pure per-line parser whose only gate is `line.trim().startsWith('@')` (:50, :55); it has no parameter for surrounding-document state and no caller supplies any. All three call sites iterate raw lines: (1) `readMemoryFileWithImports` splits on `/\r?\n/` at memory-store.ts:82 and calls the parser at :83, inlining the imported body in place at :100-106; (2) `memoryFileRecords`' `visit()` at packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:427-430 does the same raw split and additionally registers each followed target as its own `NativeCapabilitySourceRecord` of kind `memory` with `memoryImportParentPath` (:404-424); (3) packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:1003-1007 builds the pinned capability body with `.filter(line => parseMemoryImportPath(line) === null)`, so on that route a fenced `@path` line is DELETED from inside the code block rather than inlined. Measured, not inferred: a temporary bun test wrote a user MEMORY.md containing a ```text fence whose body line is `@secret.md` and called `loadMemoryPromptBlock(undefined, undefined, {userConfigDir})`; the emitted `<memory>` block was "```text / SECRET_IMPORTED_BODY / ```" — the fenced import was followed and the target inlined INSIDE the fence. Nothing upstream strips fences (`readMemoryFile` at memory-store.ts:29-33 only reads and slices to `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT`). The code-span half passes only by accident: the same probe showed `parseMemoryImportPath('`@secret.md`') === null`, but so is `parseMemoryImportPath('See @secret.md for details.')`, because the gate is line-start-only. Both live routes are reachable — the pinned capability route via base-agent.ts:976-1015, the fallback prompt route via packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts:453-455 (`capabilityContextPinned ? '' : loadMemoryPromptBlock(...)`). Fence-tracking prior art exists in the repo and is unused here: packages/shared/src/skills/storage.ts:169-176 (an `inFence` toggle) and packages/ui/src/components/markdown/linkify.ts:45-75 (`findCodeRanges`/`isInsideCode`).
divergence: This is not a wrong key name or a wrong value — the whole Markdown-awareness pass is missing. Precisely: (a) fenced code blocks are NOT skipped; a line inside ``` or ~~~ whose trimmed start is `@<path>` is followed, and the fence is corrupted — the body is spliced in on the inlining route (memory-store.ts:104-106) and the line is deleted on the pinned route (base-agent.ts:1005). (b) Code spans ARE skipped, but only as a by-product of the line-start-only gate, and that same by-product simultaneously violates memory.md:101's "anywhere in your CLAUDE.md" — no mid-line import is ever followed. So the code-span rule is currently satisfied by breaking a neighbouring rule, and any later fix that makes mid-line imports work will silently re-open the code-span hole unless a real scanner lands first. The correct unit of repair is one shared markdown-aware line scanner consumed by all three call sites, not a per-line tweak in `parseMemoryImportPath`.

change.what: Add an exported generator/array helper `scanMemoryImportLines(raw: string): Array<{ lineIndex: number; line: string; importPath: string }>` that walks `raw.split(/\r?\n/)` while tracking fenced-block state — a line whose trim starts with ``` or ~~~ toggles the state and is never itself an import; while inside a fence no line is offered to the parser (follow the `inFence` shape already at packages/shared/src/skills/storage.ts:169-176, but match the closing fence on the same marker char and a run length >= the opener so a ```` inside a ``` block does not close it, and ignore the info string). Keep `parseMemoryImportPath` (:49-64) unchanged as the per-line parser so code-span behaviour stays in one place. Rewrite the loop at :82-107 to iterate the scanner's result: only reported indices are candidates for `resolve`/`statSync`/recursive inline; every other line is pushed verbatim.

Replace the raw split loop at :427-430 with `scanMemoryImportLines(readMemoryFile(resolvedPath))`, visiting only the reported `importPath`s. Import the new helper alongside the existing `MEMORY_IMPORT_DEPTH_LIMIT, parseMemoryImportPath, readMemoryFile` block at :27-31; drop `parseMemoryImportPath` from that import if it becomes unused here. Effect: a fenced target stops producing a `memory` capability record.

Replace `.filter(line => parseMemoryImportPath(line) === null)` at :1005 with an index-based filter driven by `scanMemoryImportLines(body)` — build a `Set<number>` of the scanner's `lineIndex` values and drop only those lines, so a fenced `@path` line survives in the pinned body. Adjust the import at :25 accordingly.

change.symbol: new cases beside 'inlines @import and @path references from memory files' (:147)
change.what: Add one positive/negative pair: (1) a MEMORY.md with a ```text fence and a ~~~ fence each containing an `@target.md` line asserts the prompt still contains the literal `@target.md` and NOT the target's body, and that the fence markers survive; (2) the existing inline case at :147-167 must stay green, proving unfenced imports are unaffected. One extra case for an unterminated fence (everything after it is literal) is worth the line.

change.symbol: memoryFileRecords coverage (currently none — codegraph reports no covering tests)
change.what: Add one test asserting that a MEMORY.md whose fenced block names `@target.md` yields exactly one `memory` record (the root), with no `import-<hash>` record and no `memoryImportParentPath`.

blastRadius: Three call sites in two packages, and the change is a change in the SET of records/lines produced, so it crosses two boundaries. WIRE: native-sources records flow through `packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:968-978`, which maps `record.memoryImportParentPath` onto the runtime memory layer's `importParentPath`, which base-agent.ts:1012 emits as `parent_file_path` on the `InstructionsLoaded` hook event; a fenced target that stops being a record stops producing an `include` entry in that payload. `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/instructions-loaded.test.ts:72` asserts on `importParentPath`. PERSISTENCE: every followed import gets a capability key `memory:<scope>:<basename>:import-<sha256(relativePath).slice(0,16)>` (native-sources.ts:404-412), and enable/disable decisions are persisted by key into `CONFIG_DIR/capabilities.json` and `workspaces/<id>/capabilities.json` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/policy-store.ts:7,11); dropping fenced records orphans any stored key. Orphans are read back harmlessly as plain booleans (policy-store.ts:129-130), but this is still persisted-state drift and therefore a risk trigger under AGENTS.md's Implementation-First budget. Other readers: `loadMemoryPromptBlock` (memory-store.ts:317-334) → `packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts:455` (fallback system prompt when `capabilityContextPinned` is false); `loadUnscopedRuleMemories` (memory-store.ts:289-302). Imported Claude/Codex surfaces are in scope: `.claude/rules/` files reach the same walker via `ruleMemoryRecords` → `memoryFileRecords` (native-sources.ts:673-697, CLAUDE_RULES_DIR at :727), as do the global/session MEMORY.md entry points at :909, :978, :1027, :1092. Existing tests to keep green: packages/shared/src/agent/memory/__tests__/memory-store.test.ts and packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/__tests__/storage-runtime-fork-memory.test.ts. Note that `PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES` (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md, native-sources.ts:82) are registered by `fileRecord('instruction', ...)` and are NOT import-walked at all, so this fix does not touch them — that is a separate, larger divergence.
userImpact: Concrete and reachable today. Any MEMORY.md, `.agents/rules/*.md` or `.claude/rules/*.md` that DOCUMENTS an import inside a fenced code block — which is exactly what Claude's own memory.md does, and what any repo's "how to write memory files" section does — has that example silently executed. Measured output for a user MEMORY.md whose ```text fence contains `@secret.md`: the `<memory>` block the model receives reads "```text / SECRET_IMPORTED_BODY / ```". So the user sees (a) an instruction file that no longer says what they wrote, with a corrupted code fence, (b) an unintended file loaded into every turn's context, spending budget, and (c) in Sources, the fenced target listed as an imported memory capability they never asked for, carrying its own enable/disable toggle. On the pinned-capability route the failure is the mirror image: the fenced `@path` line is deleted, so a documentation example loses its middle line with no explanation. Worst realistic case is exfiltration-shaped: a CLAUDE.md that merely mentions `@~/.ssh/config` inside a fence pulls the file into context. The code-span half is NOT observable today — the line-start-only gate hides it — and would surface only if mid-line imports (memory.md:101, "anywhere in your CLAUDE.md") were implemented without a real scanner.
notes: Verified by execution, not only by reading: a temporary bun test at packages/shared/src/agent/memory/__tests__/f100-probe.test.ts (written, run, deleted) produced the quoted `<memory>` output and the three `parseMemoryImportPath` return values cited above. Files read in full for the cited regions: memory-store.ts (1-140, 187-334), native-sources.ts (18-110, 190-200, 360-470, 670-745, 900-985), base-agent.ts (975-1030), prompts/system.ts (445-461), resolver.ts (960-985), policy-store.ts (125-135), skills/storage.ts (163-186), ui/markdown/linkify.ts (35-80). Absence of fence/code-span state in the memory path was checked with `grep -a` over packages/{shared,ui,core}/src for inCodeBlock|insideFence|fenceState|codeSpan|inFence|fencedBlock|codeFence — only skills/storage.ts and ui/markdown/linkify.ts hit, neither on this path. Not verified: whether any Sources UI surface renders the `import-<hash>` memory records distinctly (I traced the record through resolver.ts:968-978 but did not read the renderer), and the exact CommonMark fence-nesting rules the fix should adopt — the change list proposes marker-char + run-length matching, which is CommonMark-correct but is a design choice, not something the page specifies. The doc's separate divergences visible in the same section — no mid-line imports, MEMORY_IMPORT_DEPTH_LIMIT = 5 against memory.md's "maximum depth of four hops", and the external-import approval dialog at memory.md:120 — are adjacent findings, deliberately excluded here.
